top_signals.title: Trump’s Putin Ties Draw Focus After Summit
top_signals.summary: Bloomberg Economics Analyst Alex Kokcharov tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump’s historic meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping produced limited concrete results despite a joint declaration on energy, nuclear risks and other global issues. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kokcharov explains what Trump’s relationship with Putin means for Ukraine as Europe takes on more of Kyiv’s support and the war intensifies after Ukraine’s latest attack on the Crimean Bridge. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: 'Raise Taxes, Cut Spending': Bill Dudley on the Debt
top_signals.summary: As US debt costs continue to soar, former New York Fed President Bill Dudley and Kathryn Judge of Columbia Law School discuss how to address America’s fiscal crisis, and whether Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s efforts to bring yields under control will pay off. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Wall Street Asks What Can Save AI Trade After Anthropic Wipeout
top_signals.summary: It’s been a tough month for the stock market, rocked by back-to-back punches from the stunning ouster of Jensen Huang from Nvidia Corp. and the Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterm elections.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: US Data Center Boom Faces a New Political Reality
top_signals.summary: Starting in January, Democratic governors will lead US states that together hold 77% of the 300 gigawatts (GW) of data center capacity announced for 2027-2030, including the five largest markets: Texas, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Georgia. Most of the winning candidates campaigned on making data centers pay their grid costs, rather than on stopping them, so the midterms are likely to change the terms of growth more than its pace. Our risked forecast expects 121 GW to be added in 2027-2030, including about 49 GW of the 191 GW planned for 2029-30.…
